negative_control._note: A causal strategy cannot earn a positive Sharpe on driftless data. The band reported here is the mean gross Sharpe across independent noise seeds plus and minus two standard errors; a mean landing above that band means the backtest is manufacturing return from structureless input. Net Sharpe is reported separately because a large negative net number on noise is cost drag (high turnover against zero edge), which is expected and not a leak.

leak_quantification._note: H1 has no shift to remove: its trailing-mean window already ends at t-1, so it is causal by construction and is not part of this comparison. The difference between the two columns is what a same-bar signal would have added, and it is the evidence for keeping the shift.

signal_lag_probe._note: The gate is `validated_on_noise`: with no serial dependence in the input, handing the strategy next-bar returns must score the same as the aligned mapping. `real_panel_context` shows the future-return variant scoring higher, which on real data reflects genuine momentum persistence rather than a leak -- the strategy reads only past closes, so it can benefit from persistence one day further out without having seen the future. It is reported for transparency, not as a gate.

staleness_guard.detail: The bar after a multi-day price gap exceeding max_stale_days must have a null return, while 1-day and 2-day steps remain valid; verified on both synthetic integer-day bars and UNIUSDT's 2023-01 archive gap.

embargo.rule: embargo_days = 2 x slowest feature memory, applied after the train block
embargo.note: The 180-day momentum lookback in H2's grid requires a 360-day embargo, which is more than half the 639-day locked out-of-sample window. That configuration therefore cannot be honestly scored on the locked set at all; only configurations with a short enough memory survive the rule.
